dedupe_keys.name: uk public survey of risk perception resilience and preparedness 2025

description: The UK Public Survey of Risk Perception, Resilience and Preparedness is a nationally representative survey of adults aged 18 and over that explores attitudes to emergencies and the steps people take to prepare for them. Questions cover the perceived likelihood and impact of risks such as extreme weather, 12-hour power cuts, pandemics, war and terrorist or cyber attacks on critical infrastructure, how long households could meet basic needs in a power cut that also affected gas and water supply, stored emergency items, information seen, community support and registration with utilities for priority services. The first annual survey covers over 10,000 UK adults interviewed in March and April 2025, with data tables for the UK and each of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. It is produced by the Cabinet Office and released as Official Statistics in Development: headline findings and a technical report on 23 July 2025, and supplementary sociodemographic analyses by the UK Health Security Agency's Behavioural Science and Insights Unit on 15 April 2026. Tables are free ODS spreadsheets with the full questionnaire as PDF and HTML, under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: results are self-reported and aggregated in tables, not microdata, and there is one wave so far. It supports agent-based and emergency response models of household behaviour during utility outages and cascading failure scenarios; a related record is the UK Data Service study of population response to infrastructure failure.
